chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy) from Abdullah ibn Ja'far from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Balad from his father Yahya ibn Abi al-Balad from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The miswak removes phlegm and increases intelligence.
ai.seo_question: What are the benefits of using misak according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) uniquely links oral hygiene to intellectual clarity, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the holistic purification of the body and soul. The removal of phlegm (balgham) is viewed not merely as a physical act but as a means to clear the mind, thereby enhancing wisdom (aql), which is central to Shia epistemology.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 3. Abi (rah) from Abdillah b. Ja’far from Muhammad b. al-Hussain b. Abi al-Khattab from Safwan b. Yahya from Ibrahim b. Abi al-Balad from his father Yahya b. Abi al-Balad from Abi Ja’far (a.s.) who said: “
Doing Miswak removes phlegm and increases intelligence.”
